## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from APA publisher pages (apa.org/pubs/journals/pag) and domain knowledge of APA Division 20 (Adult Development and Aging) editorial culture. Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | High |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Medium |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | High — aging × race, gender, SES, LGBTQ aging published |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Lifespan developmental psychology of aging — cognitive aging, emotional aging, socioemotional selectivity (Carstensen), successful aging, dementia precursors |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **adult / older-adult focus** with developmental-aging framework. Cross-sectional age-comparison and longitudinal designs both welcomed; longitudinal preferred for trajectory claims.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Manuscripts without adult-aging focus redirected to JEP:General or Developmental Psychology.

### Methodological Preferences

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 5 | Core |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | Mixed-methods only |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Outside scope |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | With aging-developmental focus |
| Mixed methods | 3 | Common |
| Meta-analysis | 5 | Welcomed |
| Longitudinal designs | 5 | Distinctive strength |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | 1 — APA-style third-person |
| **Expected density** | Almost none |
| **Writing style notes** | APA register; aging vocabulary (cohort, cross-sectional vs longitudinal, age-graded); growth-curve modeling reporting; cognitive-vs-emotional-vs-social aging frameworks |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewers from APA Division 20 (Adult Development and Aging) and broader gerontology community. Common demands: "Age-trajectory clarity?", "Cohort vs aging distinction?", "Longitudinal evidence?", "Generalizability across older-adult subgroups?".

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | Lifespan developmental aging psychology | https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/pag |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Medium |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Yes (strong) |
| **Discourse community signals (editorial board)** | International aging-psychology programs; APA Division 20 |

### AI-Research Notes (WO2 supplement, 2026-07-13)

> Added by `scripts/spine/patch_existing_entries.py` as a **supplementary, independent research pass** — it does NOT overwrite or supersede the Tier assessment above. Treat conflicts as a signal to re-verify, not as an automatic correction. Overall WO2 `signal_quality` for this pass: **3/5**.

**WO2 AI policy finding:** This is a publisher-wide (APA) policy, not Psychology-and-Aging-specific. Disclosure of generative AI use is mandatory (drafting, literature review assist, code, data viz all allowed with disclosure); AI-assisted copyediting for readability/style needs no disclosure; AI cannot be an author; confidential/submitted material must not be entered into AI tools by anyone in the process.

**WO2 positioning finding (what the journal accepts now):** Active special-issue CFPs (as of 2026-07) show the journal currently soliciting: (1) aging and career development/retirement (deadline 2026-09-01), (2) aging and motivation across the adult lifespan, (3) age-related changes in memory for gist vs. detail (episodic memory representational quality) — alongside its standing scope of empirical, biobehavioral, clinical, methodological, and psychosocial research on adult development/aging.

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Manuscripts without adult-aging focus
- AI use without disclosure per APA policy
- Single-cross-sectional designs without longitudinal context

### Soft Tax

Low for aging-tradition empirical authors. Long APA review cycle.

### Best Suited For

- Cognitive aging empirical research
- Emotional aging and wellbeing (Carstensen socioemotional selectivity tradition)
- Dementia precursors and cognitive-decline studies
- Social aging and relationship dynamics in later life
- Longitudinal aging designs
- Aging × diversity meta-analyses

### Not Recommended For

- Younger-adult only research (consider JPSP, Dev Psych)
- Pure clinical-dementia work (consider clinical-geriatric venues)
- Authors needing rapid turnaround

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Developmental Psychology](./developmental-psychology.md) | APA family; lifespan developmental scope |
| 2 | [Journals of Gerontology B Psychological Sciences](../psychology/journals-of-gerontology-b-psychological-sciences.md) | Gerontological Society of America peer |
| 3 | [Health Psychology](./health-psychology.md) | If aging × health |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from Developmental Psychology as "too aging-specialized," Psychology and Aging is the natural APA Division 20 home.
